clue.text: Big is beautiful

definitions.meaning: a ... sum or profit is a big, generous one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a body-positive slogan; it is two separate definitions side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: generous in size (a handsome reward) and attractive to look at.

clue.text: Issue clear in the Bard's work

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
to clear a sum after deductions is to net it

explanation.surface: A scholar finds a matter settled in one of Shakespeare's plays or poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare, the Bard, wrote 154 of these fourteen-line poems, so one is an example of his work.

clue.text: After an upset, bug gripping relative endures

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
an upset in a down clue turns a word over, so the bug's letters are read backwards

parts.note: strep is a germ, short for streptococcus, and a bug is a germ
sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: After a stomach upset, a lingering illness that also affects a family member keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' reads as an insect or a pest, but here it is a germ, the bacterium behind a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to carry on, keep going, as something that persists does.

clue.text: Case of disrepair right to bring up — that's decay

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters are used
in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a Tory is on the political right

explanation.surface: A neglected building's right side needs raising because of rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' takes D and R from disrepair; 'to bring up' turns TORY into YROT.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal rot of timber is a specific kind of decay.

clue.text: Senior politician, disaster now with him after balls-up?

indicators.note: a balls-up is a British slang word for a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A political grandee is linked to a calamity after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls-up' signals the rearrangement of DISASTER NOW HIM; 'with' and 'after' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics an opposition frontbencher who speaks on a department is a senior figure in their party.

clue.text: Scum in bathroom unit

definitions.meaning: in British slang a bunch of worthless people, a rabble, is called this
a cubicle with a spray of water for washing in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scum' suggests soap residue in the bathroom, but it is the British insult for a useless crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a contemptible group 'a right shower'; it is also the cubicle where you wash under a spray.

clue.text: Author writing stuff about Swiss canton in war — God he's extraordinary!

indicators.note: about can mean round and round, so the letters are turned around into a new order
extraordinary backs this up: the letters are put out of their ordinary order

parts.note: gear is stuff or kit, here kit for writing
Bern is a canton of Switzerland, and its capital

explanation.surface: A writer is stunned by a Swiss region at war and exclaims at a remarkable man.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul mixes a synonym and a place name into the pool with the clue's own words; 'in' is a link word, and the dash and exclamation are surface drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright of Pygmalion and Saint Joan was a celebrated writer, so a famous example of an author.

clue.text: Breaking the name of the resigned Labour leadership, it changed

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.words: the name of the resigned Labour leadership
parts.note: after the 2015 election Labour's leader Ed Miliband and shadow chancellor Ed Balls were both gone, two Eds

explanation.surface: A political commentator says a recent resignation at the top of the Labour Party changed things.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2015 Labour's leading pair, Ed Miliband and Ed Balls, both lost their posts, so the leadership's shared name gives two EDs.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has been altered or revised, so it has been changed.

clue.text: Draft list to knock up in hunting target

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned letters go within the quarry

parts.note: prey is what a hunter targets

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the two words run backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: A recruit is told to knock up a list of targets for a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROTA plus RAP into PARATOR, which goes 'in' PREY. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft version is preliminary, done in preparation for the final one, so draft can be an adjective here.

clue.text: Duty I had to enter Fleet, say, as hired capitalist?

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so these letters are put into the other piece

parts.note: the Fleet is a London river, now underground, so an example of one
a duty is a tax
I'd is short for I had, so had gives D after I

explanation.surface: A cabbie asks whether a tax went on a Fleet Street vehicle hired by a financier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fleet, which gave Fleet Street its name, is a river now buried under the British capital, so the solver needs that bit of geography.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitalist is playful: someone in the capital who is hired to drive a black cab.

clue.text: Check hinge drops from above

parts.note: to hinge on something is to rest on it, so hinge means rest
rain is water dropping from the sky

explanation.surface: An inspection finds a hinge falling from overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: To check someone is to hold them back or curb them, a synonym.

clue.text: March, some springtide month

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A calendar note: March is one of the spring months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' reads as the month, but it is the protest kind of march.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march through the streets is a demonstration, shortened to this word.

clue.text: One in the printing trade yet to be embarrassed about page on the Sun?

indicators.note: about means going round, so these letters surround the page
to be embarrassed is to be thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the sun sets every evening, so whimsically it is a setter

explanation.surface: A tabloid printer is still to blush over a page in The Sun newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be embarrassed' turns YET into TYE, which goes 'about' P. 'The Sun' looks like the newspaper but is just something that sets; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor who arranged type for printing worked in the print industry.

clue.text: See 6
A little current news not half fitting I would speculate, ultimately

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, its first two letters

parts.note: apt means fitting or suitable
I'd is short for I would

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A trader says a little up-to-date news, not quite half right, would let them speculate in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is the tide with the least range between high and low water, so a small tidal current.

clue.text: A substance injected perhaps, one shooting up?

parts.note: a steroid is a drug that may be injected, for example by athletes

explanation.surface: An athlete injecting a drug is a person who shoots up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting up' reads as injecting drugs, but here it means hurtling through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor planet or rock flying through space could loosely be one shooting about up above.

clue.text: Red film screens all orange, initially

indicators.note: screens means hides or shields, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A communist film is shown with everything tinted orange at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Chairman Mao is a communist, and Red is a common label for communists.

clue.text: Brush skimmed off something in the soup

indicators.note: something skimmed off loses its top layer, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a fox's tail is called its brush

explanation.surface: A cook skims the scum off the top of a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In hunting a fox's tail is its 'brush'; removing the top letter of FOXTAIL leaves the soup ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: This cut of beef or veal is a classic soup ingredient, giving its name to a British soup.

clue.text: Pictures of a painfully seductive nature in flier

parts.words: Pictures of a painfully seductive nature
parts.note: S and M art is imagery of sadomasochism, pleasure mixed with pain

explanation.surface: An exhibition of kinky pictures is shown in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: S and M is short for sadomasochism, so 'pictures of a painfully seductive nature' are S and M art.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown swallow-like bird, which nests in sandy banks, is a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: See 9
See 25
See 9
See 5
Human right to treasure little time

indicators.note: to treasure is to hold close, so the letter is held inside the other piece

parts.note: a moral is what is right, the lesson of a story
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A humanist says it is right to value the brief time we have.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans are subject to death, which is what being mortal means; as a noun it is a person.

clue.text: Bound to fill shot with it

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt, a try
a bound is a limit or end

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to load a gun with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain' and 'with it' looks like a link phrase; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means being up to date and fashionable.

clue.text: That's used for identifying theme song, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a unique code stamped on a product to tell one item from another
a theme tune is a musical piece, a ..., belonging to a TV drama in instalments

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful reading: a song from a serial.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carry a unique code for identification; whimsically, a song from a TV drama in episodes is one.
